properties.description:
An agent can query the design and render the two systems viewpoints a DoDAF/UAF-trained reader expects, WITHOUT extrapolating: SV-1/SvcV-1 (Systems/Services Interface Description — the parts, their boundaries, and what crosses each) and SV-4/SvcV-4 (Systems/Services Functionality Description — the system functions and the flows between them).

DISTINCT FROM epoch:the-systems-views-are-rendered-from-the-graph, which is WHEN this is due. This is WHAT must become true, and it outlives the increment that carries it.

WHOSE JOB IS WHOSE, and it is the point rather than an implementation note. reflow2 serves the content; the AGENT renders. Anthony, 2026-08-30: "this is the concept we defined a long ago that the agent would do the rendering." So the deliverable is not a new fixed renderer — `tools/render_views.py` is the standing one and already carries a "Structural ≈ SV-1" row — but whether an agent holding only the served design can produce these two views at all.

⭐ THE VIEW IS A PROBE, and docs/viewpoints.md already governs: "If rendering requires extrapolating or filling in missing details, that is a sign something is missing or wrong inside reflow2 — not a prompt to improvise." A confession list is a work list. Rule 4 of that file is the one to watch: a renderer that reaches zero confessions by asking only what the graph can already answer has been tuned to the instrument.

WHAT IS ALREADY THERE, so this is not started from nothing: Structural (≈ SV-1) and Functional (≈ OV-5) are rendered today. SV-4 IS ABSENT FROM THE CATALOGUE ENTIRELY — and it is not OV-5 renamed. OV-5 is operational activity; SV-4 is SYSTEM function and the data flowing between functions. Whether reflow2's vocabulary can express that is the open question this answers: `Capability` carries function, `DEPENDS_ON` between capabilities forms the functional DAG, and `Flow` + `PART_OF_FLOW.step_order` carries ordering — but nothing yet says what DATA crosses between two functions, which is half of what SV-4 is.

WHY IT SITS AFTER THE SEAM WORK: SV-1 is an interface description and can only be as good as the seam picture beneath it. It will confess exactly where contracts are undeclared, which makes it the honest test of whether that increment landed — and a better use of effort than hand-writing contracts for reflow2's own six uncovered boundaries, which Anthony's 2026-08-13 reasoning already rejected as fixing one design and teaching reflow2 nothing.

NOT DECIDED HERE: whether the output is HTML alongside the existing views page, a served projection, or something the agent composes per session; and whether SV-4's data-flow half needs new vocabulary or is a modelling gap in reflow2's own design only.
properties.name: The systems interface and functionality views (SV-1/SvcV-1, SV-4/SvcV-4) are rendered from the graph, and every fill-in is confessed
